claims.text: With nearly 90 percent of the votes counted by Wednesday evening, neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot appeared to have enough seats to form a government on his own.
A majority in the 120-seat Knesset requires 61 seats.
Early results put Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition bloc at about 53 to 54 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at around 49 seats.
Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party remains the largest single party in parliament, with an estimated 26 seats.
Arab citizens of Israel turned out to vote in record numbers during the election.
Gadi Eisenkot stated he wants an Israeli government that is Zionist and committed to universal military conscription.
The Israeli Knesset is scheduled to open on November 10.
Israelis rallied in Tel Aviv demanding a Jewish-Arab government after Arab parties made major gains in Tuesday's election.
The two main Arab parties in Israel are projected to win around 19 of the Knesset's 120 seats.
Yair Golan, leader of the centre-left Democrats party, called for forming a change government in partnership with Arab citizens of Israel.
Israel's Central Elections Committee received a complaint from the Likud party alleging that Arab parties compromised election integrity.
UN rights chief Volker Turk said he hopes the next Israeli government will change course massively and respect international law.
The two main Arab political parties in Israel are the Yousef Jabareen-led Joint List and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas.
Yousef Jabareen stated the Joint List would seek to use its projected 12 seats to facilitate removing Benjamin Netanyahu's government.
Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas stated that senior members of Gadi Eisenkot's bloc had discussed a potential coalition deal with him prior to the election.
Likud spokesman Guy Levy confirmed that Likud would not negotiate with any Arab party to form a government.
Arab citizens of Israel comprise approximately 20% of the population, or roughly 2.1 million people.
Voter turnout in the Israeli election on October 27 was the highest recorded since 1999.
Gadi Eisenkot's political party Yashar was formed one year prior to the 2026 election.
Riot police were deployed in Madrid as far-right demonstrators clashed with police during anti-government protests over a deadly train crash.
A collision between two high-speed trains in Spain killed at least 68 people and injured around 100.
The crash occurred when a southbound Renfe high-speed train travelling from Madrid to Seville collided with a stationary Iryo train.
Spanish trade union CSIF demanded the resignation of Transport Minister Óscar Puente, accusing him of using a railway employee as a scapegoat.
Transport Minister Óscar Puente stated that state-owned manager Adif took manual control after a safety system disruption and allowed a Renfe train to proceed despite a red signal.
Around 500 demonstrators gathered outside the Transport Ministry in Madrid on Wednesday night, throwing bottles and flares at police.
The collision occurred shortly after 09:00 GMT around 140 kilometers south of Madrid, between the municipalities of Mora and Orgaz.
The stationary Iryo train was carrying 147 passengers, while the Renfe train was carrying 397 passengers.
Far-right party Vox refused to suspend its election campaign rallies following the crash, with leader Santiago Abascal rejecting attempts to silence criticism of infrastructure.
Spain experienced a previous high-speed train disaster near Córdoba in January that killed 46 people.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of national mourning following the train disaster.
The train collision in Toledo province is the third deadliest railway incident in Spain over the last 50 years.
Spain's football federation postponed all 24 Copa del Rey matches scheduled for Wednesday.
Defeated Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro landed at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport in Florida after leaving Brazil.
Flávio Bolsonaro stated in a letter: 'I did not flee Brazil; I left for the sake of Brazil.'
Newly re-elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the runoff election by more than four million votes.
Brazilian authorities cancelled Flávio Bolsonaro's passports after he failed to surrender them within a 24-hour deadline.
Flávio Bolsonaro and his family travelled by land into Argentina, boarded a private jet in Puerto Iguazú, stopped in Guayaquil, Ecuador, and flew on to Miami.
Flávio Bolsonaro published a letter on social media declaring himself the 'elected president' of Brazil before updating it to state he is the 'leader'.
Flávio Bolsonaro is under criminal investigation in Brazil over financial crimes, corruption, and money laundering related to the unreleased film 'Dark Horse'.
Flávio Bolsonaro has held Italian nationality since 2023.
President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva called Flávio Bolsonaro's secret departure a 'shameful' act.
Flávio Bolsonaro's political party acknowledged the official results of Sunday's presidential election.
US President Donald Trump told reporters regarding the Brazilian election: 'I won't get involved. It was a very strange election, that's for sure.'
Flávio Bolsonaro is scheduled to lose his parliamentary immunity from prosecution in February when his Senate term expires.
Former president Jair Bolsonaro is in jail in Brazil on charges of leading a conspiracy to stay in power after losing the 2022 election.
Flávio Bolsonaro expressed gratitude in his letter to Argentine President Javier Milei and US President Donald Trump.
Brazil's federal police faced public criticism for failing to prevent Flávio Bolsonaro from leaving the country.
